summary: Eight experiments completed in 2.7 minutes; five were compute-bound. Three compute-bound entries tied for the longest listed duration at 1 minute, but no data available this milestone explains their phase costs.

slowest_experiments.experiment: Task-owned SOTA memory lease and artifact contract
V590 branch disposition and PRD gap update

bottlenecks_identified: GPU 0 was idle at 0% utilization while GPU 1 was at 85% during the compute-bound milestone snapshot. This left one accelerator unused.

The disk-mtime reconstruction reports whole-minute values for the listed entries. Three compute-bound entries therefore tied at 1 minute, and no data available this milestone identifies their slow phase.
The GPU snapshot detected a single Python inference process. It did not provide task-level batching, model-concurrency, or runner-identity evidence.
improvements_suggested: Batch 8-16 questions per forward pass for compute inference. The GPU report estimates a 4-8x throughput improvement.
When a task loads 2 or more models concurrently, place the second model on idle GPU 0. Do not enforce DualGPURunner for a one-model task.
Add task-owned phase timestamps, GPU samples, loaded-model count, and runner identity to each compute launch receipt. This will expose phase costs and DualGPURunner eligibility.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add automatic 8-16 question batching to the inference launcher.
Add device-aware placement for a second concurrently loaded model so GPU 0 can contribute.
Record task-scoped phase timing, GPU utilization, model concurrency, and runner identity.
meta_reflection: The 75% estimate is the lower-bound runtime reduction implied by the stated 4x batching improvement. It applies to batched inference, not the full 2.7-minute milestone, because no data available this milestone gives the batched share or explains the longest tasks. No data available this milestone establishes concurrent loading of 2 or more models or a missed DualGPURunner dispatch.
